prompt.es: Escribe un texto que compare dos fiestas con matices, una generalización y un ejemplo.

answer.text: The spring parade in Ana's city and the harvest fair in Tom's town are quite different, but both are lively. The parade is far more crowded than the fair: thousands of people come to see the colourful costumes and listen to loud music. The fair, in contrast, is nowhere near as noisy, because it has only about two thousand visitors and gentle music. The parade is also noticeably older; it is about two hundred years old, whereas the fair is only fifty. In both places, families tend to spend the day together and share food. For instance, Tom's grandmother prepares the same soup for the fair every year. Of course, not everybody follows this custom, and many visitors simply enjoy the music. In short, each festival has its own character, and neither is better than the other.
accepted: The spring parade in Ana's city and the harvest fair in Tom's town are quite different, but both are lively. The parade is far more crowded than the fair: thousands of people come to see the colourful costumes and listen to loud music. The parade is also noticeably older; it is about two hundred years old, whereas the fair is only fifty. In both places, families tend to spend the day together and share food. For instance, Tom's grandmother prepares the same soup for the fair every year. Of course, not everybody follows this custom, and many visitors simply enjoy the music. In short, each festival has its own character, and neither is better than the other.

Ana's spring parade and Tom's harvest fair are similar in some ways, but they are not the same. The parade is much bigger and slightly more expensive than the fair, and its costumes are far more colourful. However, the fair is every bit as friendly, and many visitors say it is more relaxed. Generally, families tend to cook and eat together during both festivals. For example, Ana's cousins make the same dish every spring, whereas Tom's neighbours bring bread to the fair. Not all families do this, of course, but it is a common custom. Both festivals show that traditions change from place to place, and that one festival is not better than another.

I compared two festivals: the spring parade in Ana's city and the harvest fair in Tom's town. The parade is far older than the fair, whereas the fair is slightly cheaper for families. The fair is not quite as crowded as the parade, but it is every bit as lively when the music starts. Many people in both places tend to wear special clothes and meet relatives. For instance, Tom's grandmother makes soup for the whole village, and Ana's neighbours dance in the street. These are only examples, and not everybody does the same. In general, both festivals are different ways of celebrating the same idea: being together.

prompt.es: Escribe una guía breve para visitantes: normas, consejos, comparación y respuesta.

answer.text: Welcome to the harvest fair! Visitors are supposed to respect the quiet time at noon, and it is customary to queue for food. My advice is to dress warmly and wear comfortable shoes, because the evening is much colder. The fair is nowhere near as crowded as the spring parade, so the morning is the best time to visit. Also, avoid taking photos of people without asking. Many visitors ask whether they should bring a gift to a family stall. It is not customary, but people tend to buy something from the stall instead, and the families usually appreciate it. If you are not sure about anything, ask a local. Enjoy the fair!

Hello, visitors! Here is a short guide to our harvest fair. You are supposed to be quiet at noon, and locals tend to queue patiently for food. I suggest that you dress warmly, because the evening is far colder than the afternoon. It is worth going in the morning, since the fair is nowhere near as crowded as the parade. Some visitors ask if they should give a gift to a family stall. That is not customary, but buying something is a nice way to say thank you. If you have any doubt, please ask at the information stall.

Welcome! Please respect the quiet time at noon, as visitors are supposed to. My advice is to arrive early and to check the schedule, because the parade sometimes starts late. The fair is much smaller than the parade, so it is not quite as noisy and you can talk easily. Do you need to bring a gift to a family stall? Not really: it is not expected, but people tend to buy a little food from the stall. Generally, locals are happy to help, so do not be shy and ask. I hope you enjoy the fair.
